titre: Child support and your tax return
resume: The paying parent can deduct child support, the receiving parent declares it. With shared residence, no deduction but the tax shares are split. What to keep as proof.
aQuoiCaSert: Child support paid for a child affects both parents' income tax: a deduction for one, taxable income for the other. It never appears on the pre-filled tax return: each parent must enter it themselves. Declaring it correctly, with the right proof, avoids mistakes and tax reassessments (redressements).
quiEstConcerne: The parent who pays support for a minor child who lives with the other parent.
The parent who receives the support.
The parent raising their children alone (box T).
aSavoir: Paying parent, minor child: support is deductible if the child usually lives with the other parent. With a judgment, it is the amount set (indexed), and some expenses paid directly (school canteen, schooling, medical costs) can also be deducted. Costs related to visiting rights, such as plane tickets or travel, are not deductible.
Support not set by a judgment: you can deduct the sums paid under the maintenance obligation (obligation alimentaire), provided you can prove them.

Receiving parent: support is taxable up to the amount the other parent can deduct. Declare it under "Pensions, retraites, rentes", on the line "Pensions alimentaires perçues". A 10% allowance is applied automatically.
Shared residence: no support is deductible, because each parent gets a share of the family quotient (quotient familial, the system of tax shares per household) for the child.
Box T (case T): a single, divorced or separated parent who lives alone with their dependent children ticks box T and gets an extra half share.

Adult child who does not live with you and is not attached to your tax household: proven expenses are deductible up to €6,855 per child, a ceiling raised to €13,710 in certain situations detailed on service-public.gouv.fr; the child declares the amount received.

documents.libelle: Judgment or agreement setting the support (copy)
documents.detail: Ask the court registry (greffe), the lawyer or the notary for a copy if you no longer have it.

documents.libelle: Proof of each payment during the year
documents.detail: Bank statements, transfer notices, certificate from ARIPA (the Caf's child support collection agency) if the support is paid through it. Cash without a receipt is hard to prove.

documents.libelle: Invoices for expenses paid directly for the child
documents.detail: School canteen, schooling, medical costs, if you deduct them on top of the support.

documents.libelle: Annual summary of amounts paid or received
documents.detail: Total for the calendar year. You can export it from the Lien Parental Journal.
Download it from your personal account on impots.gouv.fr.

documents.libelle: Decision or agreement setting the residence (shared or not)
documents.detail: To justify the split of shares or box T if the tax authorities ask.

etapes.titre: Add up the amounts paid or received over the calendar year
etapes.detail: The Journal (Finances filter, Pension category) gives you the history of recorded payments.

etapes.titre: Check before filling in your tax return
etapes.detail: The total matches your bank statements; the child is not declared as your dependent if you deduct the support; with shared residence you deduct nothing; the proof is stored in the Vault.
As deductible expenses if you pay it, under "Pensions alimentaires perçues" if you receive it. It is never pre-filled.

etapes.titre: Tick box T if you are raising your children alone
etapes.detail: Only if you live alone with them and are single, divorced or separated.
The tax authorities may ask for it.
